Resolves #19030
Related: #19028, #19024

`fixedWaitMs` now branches on the callee **shape** rather than one name, and the pre-parse filter admits the second token in the same edit. A `page.waitForTimeout(n)` at or above `THRESHOLD_MS` with no justification is a site; it never was before, in any tier, including the unit tier the guard has always scanned.

Evidence: L2 (guard executed against the real tree; per-gate mutation controls; 42 specs) → L2 required (all ACs are static-contract or local-execution). Residual: none within this scope.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: new arm `a waitForTimeout wait is a site, and the delay contract is shared with setTimeout` — bare and computed forms are sites at 3000; a named delay, a sub-threshold delay and a marked wait are not. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: new arm `a file whose only wait is waitForTimeout is parsed rather than skipped`. Its own arm because the second gate fails in the same direction as the first — see the mutation matrix below. |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: `node ./buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` → `OK — 56 unaccounted site(s) baselined, 0 new, 0 stale`, exit 0. **40 entries covering 53 occurrences**, plus the 3 pre-existing `setTimeout` rows. |
| AC-4 | outside-CI: both-shape controls plus the per-gate mutations below; the `setTimeout` regression control is the existing suite, unchanged at 21 arms in that file. |
| AC-5 | `check-fixed-sleeps.mjs:3-7` now states both matched shapes and keeps `THRESHOLD_MS` as the one remaining deliberate boundary, replacing the sentence that recorded the call-shape narrowing as intended. |

## Deltas from ticket

**Two numbers, two populations, and the ticket named only one.** AC-3 said "the 53 pre-existing sites are in the baseline". The baseline keys on `{file, text}`, so **53 occurrences collapse into 40 entries** — nine lines are byte-identical repeats inside a single file, four of them in `RefreshDomCorpseRepro.spec.mjs`. The census counts 53 and the baseline holds 40 rows, and neither is "the number of sites" on its own. (An earlier draft of this paragraph said *"the CLI prints 40"* — that was the transient pre-baseline listing I happened to measure, not the shipped behaviour. At this head the CLI prints **`OK — 56 unaccounted site(s) baselined`**: 53 `waitForTimeout` plus the 3 pre-existing `setTimeout` rows. @neo-gpt caught it.) I found this as a discrepancy between my own two measurements and reconciled it rather than picking the convenient one; the AC now names both.

**The computed form is admitted.** `page['waitForTimeout'](3000)` is one keystroke from the dotted form, and exempting it would reward the spelling. The receiver stays free and the method name is the key, so a helper re-exposing the call on its own object is still the same wait.

**`isSelfNamingDeadline` does not apply on the new arm** — `waitForTimeout` takes no callback, so there is nothing to inspect. The named-constant exemption is shared.

## Test Evidence

**Per-gate mutation matrix.** The two gates fail in the same direction, so "the suite reds" would not have told me which one a repair reached:

```
gate 1 disabled (callee predicate)    both new arms RED
gate 2 disabled (pre-parse filter)    gate-1 arm GREEN, gate-2 arm RED
both intact                           42 passed
```

**That matrix is also what found a defect in my own first draft.** Its fixtures for the gate-1 arm carried no `setTimeout` token, so gate 2 skipped them too and *both* arms reported the same failure under either mutation — the second arm was decorative and I could not have known from a green run. The fixtures now carry a deliberate token, stated in a comment at the point it matters, and the arms discriminate.

**A second, independent tell from the gate-2 mutation**, worth recording because it is the shape a future reader will hit first: with the token dropped, the guard does not report *fewer sites* — it reports **`2 baseline row(s) no longer match a live site`**, 2 rows in **1 file** (`RowSlotRemapDuplication.spec.mjs`) covering 3 occurrences. A silent detector gap surfaces as a loud baseline inconsistency.

Two corrections to that sentence, both @neo-gpt's. It originally said *"five **files** … stop being parsed"*, which conflated rows with files — the same population error this PR is otherwise about. And the number itself moved: he measured 5 rows across 4 files at `e100d38130`, correctly, **before** the backslash admission below. That admission now lets three of those four files through on their own backslashes, so the figure at this head is 2/1/3. Both measurements are right at their own trees.

**Baseline generation.** Written by a script that refuses to run if any pre-existing entry would be dropped; all 3 prior rows are reproduced. Burning this baseline down is explicitly out of scope and stays #19030's successor question.

**What is still not caught, and the ticket says so:** `waitForTimeout(400)` — the wait in #19024 that started this chain — is below `THRESHOLD_MS` and remains outside the guard. That is the third gap, it has its measured population in #19030's Out of Scope, and it is a threshold decision rather than a matcher one.


## Escape-language repair (`10cbbac900`)

@neo-gpt probed the exported guard at `e100d38130` and found the widened callee had outrun the pre-parse filter. A computed property is a **string**, and the string-escape language is far larger than the IdentifierName one the `\u` admission was written for. Three spellings, each verified to call the real method with `3000` and each carrying **no** `waitForTimeout` substring:

```
page['waitFor\x54imeout'](3000)        guard=[]  ->  [3000]
page['waitForTim\eout'](3000)          guard=[]  ->  [3000]
page['waitForTime\<newline>out'](3000) guard=[]  ->  [3000]
```

His isolation is the part I want to credit: adding an inert `// setTimeout` comment to the hex fixture made it report `[3000]`, which proves the gap is **gate 2** and not the callee predicate.

**The filter's own comment predicted this** — *"widening `fixedWaitMs` beyond a `setTimeout` Identifier callee invalidates this argument again"* — four lines above the line I changed. I widened the callee without re-reading the warning in the file I was editing.

The admission is now **any backslash** rather than a whitelist of escape forms: every one of those spellings needs one, and so does every form nobody has thought of yet. A conservative superset survives the next widening; a partial whitelist has to be rediscovered by a probe each time. Measured cost: **338 of 672** spec files parsed rather than 185, whole run **0.37s**.

**The two halves of gate 2 now have independent controls**, and the new arm asserts the runtime before it asserts the guard — a fixture that does not run can drift from the runtime it claims to mirror:

```
drop the waitForTimeout token   ->  plain no-token arm RED, escape arm green
revert backslash to \u          ->  escape arm RED, plain no-token arm green
both intact                     ->  43 passed
```
